body:
Redline round 3

Reviewed the whole pull request. Rounds 1 to 2 are already on this PR; this run starts at round 3.

The coverage pass over the whole pull request at 0e4a537 returned 8 candidates: 3 confirmed, 5 for the person, 0 collapsed into findings already reported or settled, 0 already tracked, 0 dropped (refuted, outside the diff or disproportionate).

The PR sends every finder and verifier field that the review body, the handoff and an inline comment's title post through postedText, and readBack undoes it exactly at intake. Tracing the escapes, the joiner reference and the decode order found no correctness defect. There are three nits: README Known limits leaves out a link cost that the follow-up spec's Evidence recorded, no check pins an escaped title on one Deferred branch, and the backslash trigger, which this PR widened from the base's backslash-before-backtick rule, is a question for you. On the rule checks: the version moves to 0.2.3 as a patch with no template change, both plans name their Docs sections, and no scheduled or queued work applies to this repository.

### Findings (0 correctness, 3 nit)

- **R3-1** · nit · low · confirmed · `README.md:106` · Known limits leaves out the broken link of an inline link whose destination holds `@x`
- **R3-2** · nit · low · confirmed · `tests/loop-test.mjs:1751` · No check pins the escaped title on the Deferred line's repository-rule branch
- **R3-3** · nit · low · confirmed · `workflows/redline-loop.js:965` · Any backslash escapes the whole text, so a namespaced line shows entities in its code spans · needs a decision

Each finding has an inline comment with the detail or, where GitHub could not anchor it, sits under Not placed inline below. Redline replies in the finding's thread, or in a PR comment that opens with its marker, once the round's fixes are committed.

### For the person

- `workflows/redline-loop.js:939` · Already tracked in #88. A newline or a lone carriage return in a summary, ref, title or For the person text, followed by a code fence at the start of the next line, ends the list and opens a code block at the top level, since CommonMark lets a fence interrupt a paragraph. With no closing fence, the block runs to the end of the body and swallows the set-aside block's `</details>`, Not placed inline and, in the handoff, `### Commits`. I traced this from the CommonMark spec but did not render it. #88's Change asks for a newline rule for posted free text, but its Done when names only the readers (`prior-findings`, `has-review`, `last-round`), so the fence case is worth adding there. The base's blockText kept newlines the same way and For the person lines were posted raw, so this PR removed no guard. The comment above setAsideBlock and docs/running.md:48 claim only that no tag can end the block.
- `workflows/redline-loop.js:951` · readBack decodes only the workflow's `@⁠`, `<` and `&`. A title posted raw by 0.2.2 or earlier that holds another entity outside a span (`>`, `"`, ` `) is reposted on a fresh 0.2.3 launch as `&gt;`, so the page shows the entity where GitHub used to show the character. Rider (a) and the PR body only talk about `<`, so nothing they claim is false. This needs an old title with a literal entity in it, so it is rare and cosmetic. postedText never writes a bare `>` outside a span, so readBack could decode named entities before `&` and stay an exact inverse for new text.
- `workflows/redline-loop.js:2963` · On the Decisions, Deferred, Left to you and Earlier rounds lines, the title goes through postedText alone and the outcome, mitigation or reply after it stays raw. So if a title leaves a backtick open, GitHub pairs it with the first backtick in that raw text. The title's `<`, `&` and `@⁠` then show as entities inside the span, and the raw text's own span breaks. It never leaks: what the title's reading left raw stays inside GitHub's span, and the owner's `decided by: @login` closes the line, so no span can hold it. The #87 spec chose this ('A field before raw text is rendered alone'). The sentence 'Fields that share a line are read as one text' at docs/running.md:137 reads wider than that, and could say it applies to the finder's and the verifier's fields.
- `workflows/redline-loop.js:939` · postedText neutralises only account mentions. A cross-repository reference such as `laravel/framework#51234` in a finder's summary or a verifier's ref still adds a backlink to that issue's timeline from every round's body and from the handoff. That happened before this PR too (the base posted the same text), and same-repository issue numbers are links Redline relies on. New with this PR: a commit reference such as `owner/repo@1a2b3c4` gets the joiner after its `@` and probably loses its link. README Known limits does not list that cost next to the email and bare URL. I did not render it.
- `workflows/redline-loop.js:107` · readBack exists because a fresh launch takes earlier titles from the posted review body. The raw titles, keyed by id, are also in each round's committed record (`<specFolder>/redline/round-<n>-findings.json`). Reading them from there would make the round trip a plain copy, with no inverse to keep in step with postedText. The #87 spec's answer 16 chose the decode at intake and kept `prior-findings` a byte-for-byte reader, and a record is on the branch only after a run pushed it. So this is a design option, not a defect.

comments.body:
**R3-1** · nit · low · confirmed

**Known limits leaves out the broken link of an inline link whose destination holds `@x`**

README Known limits (line 106) lists a bare URL's broken link as a cost of neutralised text, but leaves out the inline link. Any text holding `](` is escaped whole (textParts, workflows/redline-loop.js:965). So an `@` before a letter or digit in a link destination gets `⁠`, and GitHub decodes the reference there too. The follow-up spec's Evidence table records it: `[a](https://x.com/@⁠click)` renders with the href `https://x.com/@%E2%81%A0click`. The bare URL visibly shows `⁠`, but here the link text reads as written, so the link looks right and leads somewhere else. Examples are a scoped npm package page, a `pkg@version` CDN URL or a profile URL. An `@` in a link destination was never a mention, so the reference protects nothing there. The 'What is escaped and neutralised' bullet in docs/running.md (line 137) also names only the bare URL.

Proposed fix: Add a clause to the costs list in README.md, Known limits (line 106): an inline link whose destination holds `@x` keeps its text, but its href gets the joiner (`%E2%81%A0`) and leads to another page. Add the same clause next to the bare-URL sentence in docs/running.md, 'How the review is posted', the 'What is escaped and neutralised' bullet (line 137).

**R3-2** · nit · low · confirmed

**No check pins the escaped title on the Deferred line's repository-rule branch**

The handoff's Deferred line has two branches, and each makes its own postedText call: workflows/redline-loop.js:2967 for a finding autopilot left under a repository rule, and 2968 for a mitigation. Section 16 pins only the mitigation branch (this line). The rule branch has one check, the section 12 autopilot case at line 1045. That case scripts the plain titles 'title R1-2' and 'title R1-3', which postedText returns unchanged. So if line 2967 went back to `${d.title}`, every check would stay green, while an autopilot run under an ask rule would post a raw tag or a live mention on its Deferred line. docs/running.md:127 lists the Deferred line as escaped. The tests standard asks for escaped text to be pinned for each way it is written, and for a rule to be pinned at a second call site (agent-os/standards/testing/tests.md:10 and 13). I traced this by reading both checks and grepping for every pin of the line. The reviewer role cannot run node, so the mutation was not run. The cap comment's Still open line uses findingLine, so it shares the escaping pinned at line 1743, but no capped scenario pins the cap comment's body at all.

Proposed fix: Copy the `titled` run at tests/loop-test.mjs:1036 with `interrupt: 'autopilot'`, or extend the autopilot scenario at line 1039. Give R1-2 the title 'Field <b> renamed @config' and pin this exact line under `### Deferred (mitigated now, full fix left open)`: `- **R1-2** Field <b> renamed @⁠config: left to you under repository rule craft-config; open: By hand: fix R1-2 this way.` Run it red with postedText removed from line 2967, then green. Optionally, also pin the cap comment's Still open line with a tagged title in the capped scenario (line 410).

**R3-3** · nit · low · confirmed

**Any backslash escapes the whole text, so a namespaced line shows entities in its code spans**

textParts escapes a text that holds any backslash as a whole, code spans included (line 965). So when a line names a PHP namespace and also has a span holding `<`, `&` or an `@` identifier, the entities show inside that span. For example, the title: `App\Models\User::save` drops `<x-slot>` when `$a && $b`. It posts `<x-slot>` and `$a && $b` inside its spans, and a span holding `@csrf` shows `@⁠csrf`. The base's blockText escaped a text whole only on a newline or on a backslash directly before a backtick (the removed `` /\n|\\`/ ``). That is the only backslash that changes how GitHub pairs backtick runs: a backslash escape applies only to the next ASCII punctuation character, a backslash inside a span is literal, and a backslash before `<`, `&` or `@` costs the same in both modes. The #87 spec's brief decision 5 chose any backslash, and README Known limits (line 107) names the cost, so this is a question, not a defect. Nothing leaks either way. The #87 spec's answer 15 dropped `[` as a trigger because it is common in code talk and would escape most lines whole. A namespace is just as common in Laravel text, and that answer did not weigh it. A fix edits `workflows/`, and a relaunch of this run would then hit the problem #81 describes. Question: keep any backslash as a trigger, or narrow it back to a backslash directly before a backtick, so namespaced text keeps its spans as written?

Proposed fix: If narrowed:
- In textParts' trigger at line 965, replace the bare backslash in the character class with a backslash directly before a backtick. Keep `](`, `][`, `://`, `www.`, the carriage return and the newline.
- Add section 16 cases for a namespaced title next to a span holding `<b>`, pinned as the exact posted string with its span kept, and for a backslash before a backtick, which is still escaped whole. Add a round-trip mode for each.
- Reword docs/running.md, 'How the review is posted' (line 137), and README Known limits (line 107).

If kept: no change.

This needs a decision from the author; Redline does not decide it.
